title: The 10 Best Cordless Paint Sprayers
subtitle: Battery-powered paint and stain sprayers for furniture, fences, cabinets and trim, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: We pulled the top cordless paint sprayers from a live Amazon search and ranked 10 of them on star rating, review volume and features: a battery and charger in the box, a brushless motor, adjustable paint flow and spraying without thinning. Most of this list are handheld HVLP guns that take DEWALT 20V or RYOBI 18V batteries you may already own; the two airless sprayers from Graco and Titan cost ten times more and are built for bigger jobs.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: Tilswall Cordless Paint Sprayer Dreamer400, Fits DEWALT 20V (No Battery)
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners painting furniture, cabinets and small fences.
products.verdict: The most-reviewed cordless sprayer in the search: a light handheld HVLP gun that runs on DEWALT 20V packs, with three spray patterns and a 0 to 450 ml/min flow dial. It's sold tool-only, so it's the cheap way in only if you already own the batteries.
pros: 1,736 reviews, the most on this page
Adjustable flow from 0 to 450 ml/min and 3 spray patterns
cons: Paint must be thinned; Tilswall says so on the listing
Only 2 nozzle sizes in the box

products.name: DTEZTECH Paint Sprayer for DEWALT 20V Battery (Battery Not Included), 200W HVLP Brushless, Copper Nozzles, Adjustable Flow
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners who want four nozzle sizes for under $45.
products.verdict: The cheapest brushless sprayer on the list, with four copper nozzles, three patterns and a flow knob. Its 3.9-star rating trails the Tilswall guns, and the listing rates it for coatings only up to 40 DIN/s, so plan on thinning.
pros: 15 V low-voltage cutoff protects the battery
cons: Lowest listed viscosity limit on the page (40 DIN/s)

products.name: Tilswall Cordless Paint Sprayer Shark700, Fits DEWALT 20V (No Battery)
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners spraying bigger pieces who want fewer refills.
products.verdict: Tilswall's step-up model adds a brushless motor, a larger 1300 ml cup you can top up from the side, and a flow dial that goes to 900 ml/min. It has the highest star rating on the page.
pros: Side-feed cup refills without unscrewing the container
cons: Double the price of the Dreamer400

products.name: Graco Ultra Max Cordless Airless Handheld Paint Sprayer 17M367
products.best_for: Painting contractors who want airless results on small jobs without setting up a full rig.
products.verdict: A contractor's handheld airless sprayer that runs on DEWALT 20V batteries and, per Graco, sprays without thinning. It's fully repairable, uses standard RAC X tips, and handles water, solvent and flammable coatings.
pros: Two DEWALT 20V batteries and a charger included
Fully repairable; uses standard RAC X FFLP tips
Rated for water, solvent and flammable materials
cons: 32 oz liners mean frequent refills on big walls

products.name: TAIRDA Cordless Paint Sprayer Compatible for RYOBI 18V Battery (No Battery)
products.best_for: RYOBI ONE+ owners who want a brushless sprayer for fences, doors and furniture.
products.verdict: The most-reviewed sprayer for RYOBI 18V ONE+ batteries. It has a brushless motor, four copper nozzles and a listed 80 DIN/s viscosity limit, twice the DTEZTECH's.
pros: Handles coatings up to 80 DIN/s per the listing

products.name: onefinsh Cordless Paint Sprayer for RYOBI 18V Battery, Handheld HVLP with 3 Spray Patterns & 4 Nozzles (No Battery)
products.best_for: RYOBI ONE+ owners who want a complete set of cleaning and masking extras.
products.verdict: A second RYOBI 18V option with a slightly bigger 1200 ml cup and a fuller accessory bag: ten strainers, masking film and gloves. It rates a little higher than the TAIRDA on fewer reviews.
pros: Ships with 10 strainers, masking film, gloves and cleaning tools

products.name: Titan ControlMax 1650 18V Cordless HEA Paint Sprayer with Low Overspray
products.best_for: Contractors and serious DIYers staining sheds, pergolas and playsets far from an outlet.
products.verdict: A cordless airless rig with a 1.25-gallon tank you can wear as a backpack, carry or set on the ground. Titan says each 2Ah battery sprays up to 350 sq ft, and the batteries fit Bosch 18V tools through AmpShare.
pros: HEA tips cut overspray by up to 55% per Titan
Batteries work with Bosch 18V AmpShare tools

products.name: NANWEI Cordless Paint Sprayer with 2 Batteries, HVLP Spray Gun with 1200ML Container, 4 Nozzles and 3 Patterns
products.best_for: First-time sprayer buyers who don't own DEWALT or RYOBI batteries.
products.verdict: The cheapest complete kit here: the sprayer, two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger for $59.99. It's our Best Overall because you can start spraying out of the box without owning a battery platform, for less than most tool-only guns plus a pack.
pros: Two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger included
Listed for coatings up to 80 DIN/s
cons: Batteries are NANWEI's own, not a major tool platform
No flow control or brushless motor listed

products.name: LIVIVISTA Cordless Paint Sprayer Compatible with DEWALT 20V MAX Battery (No Battery)
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners who want the most nozzle sizes and the largest cup.
products.verdict: The best seller in this search at 500+ a month. It has the biggest cup of the handhelds, six brass nozzles, an adjustable pickup tube, an LED light, and a blower attachment for dusting the surface first.

products.name: PEMMKORE Cordless Paint Sprayer, 32000RPM Spray Paint Gun with 2x4000mAh Battery
products.best_for: Buyers who want a kit with the widest nozzle range, down to 0.5 mm for fine detail.
products.verdict: A complete kit with two batteries, a charger, a 1400 ml cup, six brass nozzles and an LED light. It sells 400+ a month, but costs $25 more than the NANWEI kit for a similar package.
pros: Two batteries, charger and LED light included
Listed runtime of up to 25 minutes per battery

avoid.name: PUCAITR 1200W Cordless Paint Sprayer Battery Powered HVLP Paint Gun Kit
avoid.verdict: Its headline number doesn't hold up: 1200 W from two small 20V 2.0Ah packs isn't physically workable, and the listing also says it's compatible with Makita while shipping its own batteries. The NANWEI kit costs $5 more and includes twice the battery capacity.
reasons: The listing claims a 1200 W motor powered by 20V 2000mAh batteries. A 20V 2.0Ah pack holds about 40 watt-hours, so a true 1200 W draw (about 60 amps) would empty it in roughly two minutes and is far beyond what a compact pack can deliver.
The item highlight says 'Compatible with Makita', but the kit ships with two PUCAITR 20V batteries; the listing never names which Makita packs fit.
It has 3 nozzles where most sprayers here have 4 to 6, and its 3.1-star rating is lower than all 10 ranked picks.
The NANWEI kit costs $59.99 with two 4.0Ah batteries, double the capacity, plus a fourth nozzle.

buyers_guide.q: HVLP or airless: which cordless sprayer do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Handheld HVLP guns (most of this list, $40 to $100) blow low-pressure air to atomize paint. They're good for furniture, cabinets, doors and fences, but most need thinned paint and refill every quart or so. Cordless airless sprayers like the Graco Ultra Max and Titan ControlMax pump paint at high pressure, cover faster and handle thicker coatings, but cost $600 and up.

buyers_guide.q: Do I have to thin the paint?
buyers_guide.a: With almost every handheld HVLP here, yes. Use the viscosity cup in the box and thin until the paint runs through in the time the manual gives. The listing's DIN/s rating tells you how thick a coating it can take: 80 DIN/s handles more than 40 DIN/s. Of the sprayers on this page, only the Graco Ultra Max is sold as spraying without thinning.

buyers_guide.q: Will a 'compatible with DEWALT' sprayer void anything or damage my batteries?
buyers_guide.a: These are third-party tools built to fit DEWALT 20V or RYOBI 18V packs; DEWALT and RYOBI don't make or warrant them. Most include a low-voltage cutoff so they won't over-drain the pack. Check the listing's battery list: both Tilswall listings say they don't fit DEWALT POWERSTACK batteries.

buyers_guide.q: Tool-only or a kit with batteries?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own DEWALT 20V or RYOBI 18V batteries, a tool-only sprayer is the cheapest option. If you don't, a kit like the NANWEI ($59.99 with two batteries and a charger) costs less than buying a tool-only sprayer plus a name-brand battery and charger. Kit batteries are usually proprietary and won't run other tools.

buyers_guide.q: How long does a battery last when spraying?
buyers_guide.a: Runtime depends on battery size and the motor. PEMMKORE lists up to 25 minutes per 4.0Ah battery, and Titan rates each 2Ah pack at about 350 sq ft per charge on the ControlMax. Bigger packs run longer, so a 4.0Ah or 5.0Ah battery is worth it for fences and decks.

buyers_guide.q: How do I keep a cordless sprayer from clogging?
buyers_guide.a: Strain the paint, thin it to the right viscosity, and clean the sprayer right after you finish. Tilswall says to clean within 15 minutes. Spray water (or the right solvent) through it, take the nozzle apart, and clear the air hole with the needle that comes in the box.
